A1.justification: Both 82-page PDFs describe the same work and include Appendices A–D. Readable text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and benchmark experiments in Figures 1–3, Table 1, and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation and benchmark results, including the extensive experimental appendices.

M1.justification: The benchmark diagnostic, predictor construction, model architectures, and ColoredMNIST generation algorithm remain unchanged. The mathematical revisions do not document an altered training or evaluation algorithm.

E1.justification: The same Gaussian/mixture simulations and vision and language benchmarks are evaluated in Section 4 and Appendices B–C. No dataset, domain, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the same domain-general and domain-specific logistic regressions in the simulations and retain the same predictor families in the benchmark experiments. No comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Leave-one-domain-out splits, probit-transformed accuracy, Pearson correlation, and Table 2 model-generation settings are unchanged. Appendix B retains 50 simulated test domains and 1,000 samples per domain.

E4.justification: The interpolation/extrapolation simulations, ColoredMNIST case study in Appendix B.1, and dataset- and group-specific analyses in Appendix C retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: The empirical tables retain the same p-value and standard-error reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical estimation information is added or revised; the concentration-bound edits concern theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: The empirical values and plotted findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 1 retains Pearson R = -0.74 for ColoredMNIST Env 2 and R = 0.87 for WILDSFMoW Env 5, matching the corresponding appendix tables.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and Appendices A.2, A.5, and A.6 replace covariance factors in concentration conditions with the squared Euclidean norm of w_spu. Appendix A.1 adds the condition w_spu^T z_spu != 0 within the proof. Appendix A.7 changes its assumption from sub-Gaussian to Gaussian features and removes kappa factors from several derived expressions. These are localized revisions to existing conditions and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1 contributions, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about benchmark misspecification, accuracy on the line, and implications for benchmark selection and design.

C2.justification: Appendix A.7 now restricts its exceptional coexistence example to Gaussian rather than general sub-Gaussian features, narrowing that example's stated applicability. The main benchmark interpretations, recommendations, Section 4.4 limitations, and Appendix D discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same simulation recipes, preprocessing instructions, architecture and hyperparameter tables, and fine-tuning details. The printed code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix C.8 replaces the Camelyon reference Bandi et al. (2018) with the FMoW reference Christie et al. (2018). Both works were already cited elsewhere; the bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to version/date text, conclusion quotation marks, and minor lemma-heading formatting. There is no substantial rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: Reformatted equations, particularly Equation 11, produce limited line and page reflow. Figures and tables retain their structure, captions, axes, legends, and numbering; none is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision by replacing matrix-valued covariance factors with scalar, weight-dependent terms in central concentration bounds and making the missing nonzero projection condition explicit in the Lemma 1 proof. It also corrects the FMoW attribution. The theoretical repair remains limited: Appendix A.7 retains kappa in Equation 36 while dropping it in subsequent expressions. With empirical evidence and main conclusions unchanged, the net improvement is modest.
